data.why: the repo ships proxy records (pCO2, pH, d13C) and an emission-pulse file in dat/ for the exact inverse-model twin experiments described in the README; no synthetic data is needed.

goals: spin up a preindustrial or PETM steady-state initial condition (y0) with the forward model and verify it has converged
run a forward perturbation experiment with a chosen carbon emission pattern, amount, duration and isotopic signature, and inspect resulting pCO2, d13C, pH and CCD trajectories
invert proxy pCO2/d13C/pH records (e.g. Gutjahr 2017 PETM, Wu 2023 PTB, or Chen 2022 datasets) to recover the time-dependent carbon emission scenario fcinp(t) and its d13C
run an inverse twin experiment: generate synthetic 'truth' data from a forward run (pulse_emi.dat) and recover it via inversion to validate the algorithm
smooth noisy proxy time series with the LOWESS tool before using them as inversion targets
compare modeled vs. observed pCO2, d13C and pH to judge whether a candidate emission scenario explains a paleoclimate carbon-cycle event

review.summary: The tree is honest and well evidenced for smoothing and forward runs, and its goal matches the README's purpose. But the inverse half, which is the tool's main contribution, is just a dropdown, and the spin-up stage is missing. File it after a run that adds steady-state spin-up and a successful inversion with its results, and after the few label fixes listed.
